name: Zero Trust
certifications: CSA Certificate of Competence in Zero Trust (CCZT)
tools: Cloudflare Zero Trust (Access, Gateway, Tunnel, WARP)

beginner.summary: For IT administrators, network and security engineers and architects who know traditional perimeter security (VPNs, firewalls, Active Directory) and are new to Zero Trust. Covers the NIST SP 800-207 tenets and logical components, the CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model pillars and stages, protect surfaces and transaction flows, phishing-resistant MFA and signal-based conditional access, device posture, least privilege, ZTNA compared with VPNs, a first Cloudflare Tunnel and Access deployment, secure web gateway filtering, segmentation and mutual TLS concepts, data classification, access telemetry, a maturity self-assessment and a capstone that puts one internal app behind identity- and device-aware access.
prerequisites: Explains how a corporate network, VPN, firewall and Active Directory or another directory work together today
Understands TCP/IP, DNS, HTTPS and certificates at the level of reading a browser certificate chain
Has a laptop, a free Cloudflare account with a test domain, and a Microsoft Entra ID or Okta developer tenant with admin rights
outcomes: Explain the NIST SP 800-207 tenets, the PE/PA/PEP model and the CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model pillars and stages
Map a protect surface, its transaction flows and the identity, device and network signals an access decision needs
Configure phishing-resistant MFA, a device-aware conditional access policy and a ZTNA-published private application
Collect access-decision logs and score a starting maturity baseline for an organisation

days.topic: Zero Trust Principles and the NIST SP 800-207 Tenets
subtopics: Why perimeter trust fails: flat networks, stolen VPN credentials and lateral movement
The seven tenets of NIST SP 800-207
Resources: users, devices, services and data treated alike
Per-session access and no implicit trust from network location
Dynamic policy using identity, device state and behaviour
Continuous monitoring of asset integrity and security posture
Strict, dynamic authentication and re-authorisation
Collecting telemetry to improve policy over time
Forrester ZTX and John Kindervag's original Zero Trust model
Zero Trust as a strategy, not a single product
days.lab_task: Read NIST SP 800-207 section 2.1 and list the seven tenets in your own words. For each tenet, write one current control in a sample company (VPN, AD, firewall) that violates it and one control that would satisfy it. Then trace a real breach pattern (phished VPN password to lateral SMB movement) and mark the exact step where each tenet would have stopped it.
days.deliverable: Tenet gap table (7 rows) plus an annotated breach timeline
checks: Compare the tenet table with SP 800-207 section 2.1
All 7 tenets appear and none is merged or missing
At least 3 distinct steps are marked with the tenet that would block them
Ask the learner why network location is not a trust signal
Answer cites tenet 2: all communication is secured regardless of network location
objectives: List and explain the seven SP 800-207 tenets
Identify implicit trust in a perimeter design
Link Zero Trust tenets to real attack paths

days.topic: Policy Engine, Policy Administrator and Policy Enforcement Point
subtopics: The control plane and data plane split in SP 800-207 section 3
Policy Engine (PE): the trust algorithm and grant/deny decision

days.lab_task: Draw the SP 800-207 Figure 2 component model for two real products: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access protecting Exchange Online, and Cloudflare Access protecting a web app. For each, label which component is the PE, PA and PEP, and list at least 5 policy information sources it consumes. Then walk one request end to end and number every hop from client to resource.
days.deliverable: Two labelled component diagrams with a numbered request walkthrough
checks: PE/PA is Entra ID and the PEP is the Exchange Online or token-issuance gate
Count policy information sources per diagram
Each diagram lists 5 or more sources such as sign-in risk, device compliance and location
Entra is labelled contextual and criteria-based, with the reason written beside it
objectives: Name and separate the PE, PA and PEP roles
Identify policy information points feeding a decision
Map commercial products onto the NIST logical model

intermediate.summary: For security and platform engineers who completed the beginner level or already run MFA, conditional access and a pilot ZTNA service. Covers attribute- and risk-based policy design, externalised authorization with Open Policy Agent, Conditional Access at scale with authentication strengths and Continuous Access Evaluation, device trust from Intune and Okta, Zscaler Private Access, Microsoft Entra Private Access and Cloudflare Access with device posture, microsegmentation for Kubernetes and virtual machines, SPIFFE/SPIRE workload identity, service mesh mTLS from a Zero Trust angle, secretless CI/CD federation, short-lived SSH certificates, data loss prevention, SIEM detections, VPN-to-ZTNA migration planning and access-denial troubleshooting, ending with a VPN replacement capstone.
prerequisites: Completed the beginner level or has deployed MFA, a Conditional Access policy and one ZTNA-protected app
Administers Linux and Windows hosts and can run kubectl, Docker and a shell script
Has lab access to a Kubernetes cluster (kind or k3d is fine), an Entra ID or Okta tenant and a Cloudflare or Zscaler trial
outcomes: Design and test attribute- and risk-based access policies in Conditional Access, Cloudflare Access, ZPA and OPA
Deploy microsegmentation and SPIFFE-based workload identity with mTLS for service-to-service traffic
Remove long-lived secrets from CI/CD and admin access using federation and short-lived certificates
Plan and execute a staged VPN-to-ZTNA migration with monitoring and troubleshooting runbooks

advanced.summary: For security architects, platform leads and programme owners who run Zero Trust controls in production and must scale them across clouds, workloads and the organisation. Covers NIST SP 800-207A identity-tier and network-tier policy for cloud-native apps, the NCCoE SP 1800-35 example builds, PDP availability and fail-closed design, the policy-as-code lifecycle, risk-adaptive access, the OpenID Shared Signals Framework with CAEP and RISC, SPIFFE federation, identity propagation across microservices, OT and IoT, non-human identities, key management and attribute-based data access, third-party access, break-glass resilience, authorised adversary testing, maturity metrics, the DoD Zero Trust strategy, governance, compliance mapping and a multi-year roadmap capstone.
prerequisites: Completed the intermediate level or has run ZTNA, conditional access and microsegmentation in production
Reads and writes infrastructure and policy code (Terraform, Rego, YAML) and works with Kubernetes in more than one cloud
Has authority or a sponsor to engage application owners, risk management and leadership on a Zero Trust programme
outcomes: Design multi-cloud Zero Trust architectures using SP 800-207A identity-tier and network-tier policies and federated workload identity
Engineer resilient, tested policy decision points and policy-as-code pipelines with fail-closed behaviour and break-glass paths
Extend Zero Trust to shared signals, non-human identities, OT and IoT, third parties and data-level controls
Measure maturity with metrics, map controls to compliance frameworks and present a funded multi-year roadmap
